ai.title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.14005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the accelerated pace of AI development, any benchmark whose difficulty is calibrated with humans or current AI systems becomes circular, or saturates soon. How can we then evaluate machines that may become more capable than the current machines and the people who write the tests? One answer to the question hinges on inverse problems, inductive inference questions for which difficulty depends on the complexity of the underlying mechanism, given the observations and the previous knowledge. Levin's Kt, a computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity, puts a theoretical upper bound to that difficulty, balancing the simplest representation encoding for the mechanism and the logarithm of the time steps to run that mechanism. Previous tests derived from Levin's Kt, such as the original C-test, are based on minimalistic Universal Turing Machines (UTM), capable of very limited representations and no previous knowledge. Reasoning large language models (LLM) are UTMs that capture a compendium of human culture as knowledge, using prompts as natural language programs. This paper presents the first test based on Levin's Kt with LLMs as representational machines. Fresh test items can be produced at high difficulties, estimated in a ratio scale measured in bits, before any human or frontier model can solve them. ai.title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.14277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.

Existing approaches rely primarily on in-context personalization, parametric adaptation, or personalized reward modeling, but respectively incur recurring costs in context management, model optimization and deployment, or multi-candidate generation and scoring. ai.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.19210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). Our formulation allows pre-trained attention layers to be replaced without training a new language model from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Titan-Llama raises accuracy over segmented attention windows from 23.87\% to 40.51\% on QuALITY and from 14.50\% to 40.75\% on LongHealth. Inference benchmarks show more than 20\% faster prefill, 37\% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24\% lower steady-state decode memory usage in the evaluated configurations. ai.title: Beyond Corrected Actions: Training LLM Agents on Textual Critiques
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.19367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for multi-turn agentic tasks that require interactions with users and environments over extended sequences of actions. A common approach to improving LLM agents is to use more capable expert models to provide training supervision, either by behavior cloning the expert's trajectories or by using the expert to correct the actions in trajectories generated by the weaker student model. However, expert LLMs can provide richer supervision than actions alone: they can directly generate textual critique that explain why specific actions are incorrect. We study whether training on such feedback benefits LLM agents and propose Critique-Augmented Agentic Fine-Tuning (CAFT), a framework that elicits textual expert feedback on student-generated trajectories. For each incorrect action, the expert yields both a corrected action and a textual critique explaining the student's mistake--which we then use as the training target for fine-tuning. Across four student models from the Nemotron 3 and Gemma 4 families on the agentic domains $\tau^2$-Bench Airline+Retail and WebShop, adding critiques to action-level supervision improves performance by 8% on average over action-only distillation. Additionally, CAFT checkpoints can also provide a better warm start for reinforcement learning than expert-trajectory distillation. ai.title: Moral Combat: Exploiting Moral Foundations Theory to Jailbreak LLMs
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.19587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Social psychology has long described how people can be persuaded to interpret a harmful act as moral. Recent research suggests that Large Language Models (LLMs) echo aspects of human psychology, from cognitive biases to social conformity. This raises a question with direct safety implications: can LLMs be moralized to bypass safety guardrails? We answer this question with a multi-agent framework grounded in Moral Foundations Theory (MFT). Given a harmful request that is initially refused, our agents diagnose which moral foundation (MF) the prompt is violating, identify a justifiable foundation under which the same request appears virtuous, rewrite the prompt accordingly, and reinforce it with generated precedents of comparable moral reframing. We evaluate our framework on harmful prompts from three well-known jailbreak datasets across five open-source and proprietary models. Our analysis reveals that models are highly susceptible to moralization, exhibiting high single-trial jailbreak rates with success increasing further under repeated attempts. We also find that safety benchmarks are imbalanced in the MFs they violate, concentrating on foundations toward which models already exhibit biases.
ai.summary: Social psychology has long described how people can be persuaded to interpret a harmful act as moral.

ai.raw_summary: Commission holds special meeting of Scientific panel on frontier AI safety and risks Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 10/09/2026 - 09:16 The Commission holds a special meeting of the Scientific Panel on artificial intelligence (AI). The panel has been investigating recent loss-of-control incidents, and together with the Commission’s AI Office, has worked on a set of questions for the companies that developed the models involved. Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, will attend the meeting. The Scientific Panel brings together 60 world-leading independent experts who advise the EU AI Office and national authorities on systemic risks, model classification, evaluation methodologies, and cross-border market surveillance. During the meeting, the panel will present recommendations to the Commission on frontier AI safety and security risks. Executive-Vice President Henna Virkkunen said: “The EU has the first law in the world that addresses systemic risk from AI, and we need state-of-the-art scientific input. AI capabilities are advancing rapidly, but with a strong legal framework, decisive enforcement and the best scientific minds supporting this work, Europe can lead in ensuring safe and secure AI.” Find out more about the Scientific P anel on artificial intelligence (AI) Related topics Artificial intelligence AI Office Scientific panel Related content News article 12 October 2026 Special meeting of the AI Scientific Panel On 9 Octobe

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases. The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) reduced its workforce by 29 percent in 2025 and modified the types of programs it funds in response to presidential directives and executive branch guidance. HUD largely achieved workforce reductions through deferred resignation programs. Over half the employees who separated had at least 10 years of service at HUD, including 41 percent with more than 20 years of service. HUD did not publish notice of any reorganization plans that led to field office closures in 2025, though in 2026 it announced plans to consolidate one field office into a nearby regional office. HUD also terminated about 21 percent of its active contracts in 2025, valued at about $367 million. Most terminated contracts involved professional or IT services. ai.title: Federal Law Enforcement: CBP and ICE Should Improve Body-Worn Camera Program Management
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Body-worn cameras provide law enforcement personnel with the capability to record interactions with the public. When initiating their body-worn camera programs, the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) each developed a plan that included key components of a comprehensive program management plan. However, CBP and ICE have not updated their program plans since 2022 and 2024, respectively. They have therefore not taken into account significant changes in the program, such as increases in the number of cameras scheduled for deployment and a 2025 pause in further camera deployment. Body-Worn Camera and Functional Buttons CBP and ICE have stated desired results for their programs, including enhancing officer safety, transparency, accountability, and public trust. Although CBP and ICE implemented some measures to track information about camera availability and reliability, they have not implemented results-oriented performance goals and measures. Doing so would help them assess the results of their body-worn camera programs. For example, potential goals and measures might involve use of footage in use of force investigations. CBP and ICE have established policies related to camera use and the management of footage and implemented related oversight mechanisms to help ensure compliance with policy. trade.raw_summary: 經濟部今（12）日召開貿易救濟審議會，會中就我國對越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品反傾銷案之產業損害初步調查結果進行審議，認定有合理跡象顯示國內產業遭受實質損害。後續將移請財政部進行傾銷調查。 經濟部表示，本案調查資料涵蓋期間（112年1月至115年6月），越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品進口量自113年至114年大幅增加，進口價格逐年下降，且皆低於國產品內銷價格。國產品為與之競爭不得不跟進減價，減價幅度更甚於涉案貨物，惟因內銷價格仍高於涉案傾銷貨物致流失客戶，即便我國需求有所成長時也不見改善，導致市場占有率持續下降及內銷虧損擴大，國內產業營運狀況持續惡化；至115年1-6月因申請人宣布即將申請反傾銷調查，加上價差縮小，國內產業各項經濟指標，包括內銷虧損情形始不致繼續惡化。顯示越南特定冷軋不銹鋼扁軋鋼品傾銷進口對國內產業造成不利影響。 依據「平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法」規定，我國反傾銷案件調查由財政部與經濟部分工，分別負責「傾銷」調查與「損害」調查。程序上先由經濟部進行產業損害初步調查，如認定成立，則移請財政部進行傾銷「初步」及「最後」調查，如其「最後」調查認定傾銷成立，再由經濟部進行產業損害「最後」調查，最終交由財政部決定是否課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部將產業損害初步調查認定結果通知財政部後，財政部應於通知送達之翌日起70日內作成有無傾銷的初步認定，並決定是否臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 經濟部表示，本案如須進行產業損害「最後」調查，經濟部將就國內產業狀況進一步瞭解及查證，並蒐集各方針對課徵反傾銷稅對下游產業等國家整體經濟利益影響之意見，提供財政部關稅稅率審議小組參考。屆時並不排除其他任何新增不同事實與分析，而獲致不同的結論。 有關產業損害初步調查報告公開版可於今(115)年11月12日起至貿易署網站（網址：https://www.trade.gov.tw/）「經貿往來」/「我國採行之貿易救濟措施」/「案件調查」項下之「調查報告」下載。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：綜合企劃組邱組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7361

trade.raw_summary: 財政部 公告 發文日期：中華民國115年10月13日 發文字號：台財關字第1151027218號 附件： 主旨：力麟科技股份有限公司申請對自中國大陸產製進口特定聚醯胺薄膜課徵反傾銷稅、臨時課徵反傾銷稅及回溯課徵反傾銷稅案，經本部初步認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，自115年10月19日起臨時課徵反傾銷稅。 依據：平衡稅及反傾銷稅課徵實施辦法（下稱實施辦法）第12條至第14條，及本部關稅稅率審議小組115年9月24日第72次會議決議。 公告事項： 一、本部關稅稅率審議小組第72次會議決議略以：本案依據經濟部產業損害初步調查結果，認定有合理跡象顯示，涉案傾銷進口產品對國內產業造成實質損害，且我國產業在調查期間將繼續遭受損害；復經本部初步調查認定部分涉案廠商有傾銷情事，爰依實施辦法第13條規定，對相關涉案廠商之涉案產品臨時課徵反傾銷稅，為期4個月。 二、本案臨時課徵反傾銷稅之範圍、對象、稅率及期間如下： (一)課徵範圍： １、貨品名稱：特定聚醯胺薄膜（Certain Polyamide Film）。 ２、貨品範圍：以重量計含超過50%之聚醯胺-6，不論其表面是否經印刷、塗覆以任何材料或進行任何表面處理，未切或已切成長方形，但未經進一步加工之薄膜或箔。 ３、貨品規格： (１)厚度：0.0114公厘（含）以上至0.0315公厘（含）以下。 (２)寬度：超過5公厘。 (３)排除項目：具下列任一成分或特性之薄膜，不屬涉案貨物： 甲、薄膜表面含有金屬成分者。 乙、攝氏20度至23度且相對溼度50%至65%之測試條件下，薄膜厚度為0.015公厘時，氧氣穿透率小於15mL/(m?·day·atm)，即小於15毫升/(每平方公尺·每日·1標準大氣壓的純氧)者。 ４、參考貨品分類號列：39209229105及39209229203。 ５、用途：應用於食品、化學用品、醫療（藥）用品與電子材料包裝等。 (二)課徵對象： １、輸出國或產製國：中國大陸。 ２、國外製造商及出口商：昆山運城塑業有限公司、運城其龍新材料有限公司、鶴山運城新材料有限公司、廈門長塑實業有限公司、福建長塑實業有限公司、滄州東鴻制膜科技有限公司、滄州東鴻包裝材料有限公司、重慶明珠塑料有限公司、德州東鴻新材料有限公司、蕪湖明珠制膜科技有限公司、曉星化纖（嘉興）有限公司及佛山佛塑科技集團股份有限公司。 ３、國內進口商：慕明企業有限公司、展仝企業有限公司、建?股份有限公司及光展應材股份有限公司。 ４、其他未列名之涉案貨物製造商、出口商或進口商。 (三)臨時課徵稅率： １、昆山運城塑業有限公司（製造商）、運城其龍新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）及鶴山運城新材料有限公司（關聯製造商）：0%。 ２、其他製造商或出口商：40.21%。 ３、前揭個別廠商之臨時課徵稅率，係依其於調查期間提供資料計算決定，故涉案貨物須由該等廠商於該國生產製造並直接出口至我國，始得適用。 (四)課徵期間：依據實施辦法第13條第3項規定，臨時課徵之反傾銷稅，其課徵期間最長為4個月；如經占涉案貿易額相當比例之國外出口商請求，得延長為6個月。 三、本案尚須進行傾銷最後調查，依實地查核結果或其他新事證，可能獲致不同之傾銷差率或作成不同結論。 四、本案後續調查程序：依據實施辦法第14條及第16條規定，本部初步認定之案件，應於初步認定公告之翌日起60日內完成有無傾銷之最後認定。經最後認定有傾銷事實者，本部應即通知經濟部。經濟部應於接獲通知之翌日起40日內，作成該傾銷是否損害我國產業之最後調查認定並通知本部。本部應於接獲經濟部通知之翌日起10日內，提交關稅稅率審議小

trade.title: Investigation Into Conditions Affecting Shipping in the Foreign Trade and Denial of Entry of Vessels Into Spanish Ports and Proposed Remedies To Meet or Adjust the Unfavorable Conditions
trade.raw_summary: The Federal Maritime Commission (Commission) proposes to adjust or meet unfavorable shipping conditions created by the Government of Spain. The Commission proposes a per-voyage fee on all Spanish vessels of $200,000 and restrictions on the import of certain Spanish goods into the United States. The Commission also proposes using additional statutory authority to impose these remedies because the Government of Spain has unduly impaired the access of U.S. flag vessels to trade between foreign ports. The Commission herein offers an opportunity for a public hearing. The Commission invites public comment on all aspects of this proposed rule.

trade.title: 電動車輛自116年1月1日起得具結免徵貨物稅出廠或進口
trade.raw_summary: 為減輕完全以電能為動力之電動車輛（下稱電動車輛）產製廠商或進口人先徵貨物稅後退稅之資金積壓壓力及稅捐稽徵機關作業負荷，財政部於115年8月18日修正發布貨物稅稽徵規則第54條之1、第54條之2及第59條之1條文，增訂產製廠商或進口人於電動車輛出廠或進口前，得分別向所在地國稅局或進口地海關申請核准適用具結免稅出廠或進口放行，俟完成申領牌照登記後，再辦理銷案（下稱具結免稅事後銷案），並定自116年1月1日施行。 財政部南區國稅局說明，現行電動車輛依貨物稅條例第12條第4項及第12條之3第2項規定減免徵貨物稅，實務作業係由產製廠商或進口人於電動車輛產製出廠或進口時，先依規定稅率減半報繳貨物稅，俟消費者購買並完成申領牌照登記後，再申請退還貨物稅，採「先徵後退」方式辦理。此作業方式不僅造成廠商資金積壓，也增加國稅局及海關徵收、審理與退稅等稽徵成本，透過本次修正，改採具結免稅事後銷案作業方式，可大幅減輕廠商的依從成本。 該局舉例說明，以進口完稅價格200萬元、馬力208.8HP（汽缸排氣量在2,001cc以上）之電動小客車為例，依原作業規定進口時須先按30%稅率減半繳納30萬元貨物稅（=200萬元×15%），俟消費者購買該車輛並完成申領牌照登記後，進口人始可向進口地海關申請退還21萬元貨物稅（按貨物稅條例第12條之3第2項但書規定，電動小客車免徵金額以完稅價格140萬元計算之稅額為限，超過部分不予免徵，故退還140萬元×15%之貨物稅），實際負擔9萬元貨物稅（=30萬元-21萬元）。貨物稅稽徵規則修正後，經核准適用具結免稅事後銷案之業者，進口前開電動車輛僅須繳納9萬元貨物稅［=(200萬元-140萬元)×15%］，大幅減輕納稅義務人資金積壓負擔。 該局進一步說明，適用具結免稅事後銷案之產製廠商或進口人，應於電動車輛出廠或進口放行之次月1日起算1年內，完成申領牌照登記，並向主管稽徵機關或進口地海關辦理銷案，如無法於規定期限內辦理銷案者，應申請延期銷案或先行補繳貨物稅，否則將遭補徵貨物稅並取消適用具結免稅事後銷案資格。業者如有相關疑義，可洽所在地國稅局或進口地海關詢問，或撥打國稅局免費服務電話0800-000-321洽詢。 新聞稿聯絡人： 銷售稅組 杜組長 06-2221041
